unsupported_claims: The paper describes node2vec as running on a single machine rather than a distributed cluster.
The phases were parallelized across the cores of one multi-core, shared-memory machine, with the graph held in RAM.
The reference implementation is in Python, using Gensim's word2vec-style SGD.
The scalability experiments used a 16-core machine with 60+ GB of RAM.
rationale: The question is unanswerable from the evidence, which gives no hardware or runtime details, only that the phases are parallelizable and asynchronous. The answer invents specifics (single machine, shared memory, Python/Gensim, 16 cores, 60+ GB RAM) and never says the papers do not report this, so the core of the answer is unsupported.
